subject_label: Lithium (carded): inhibition of inositol monophosphatase as the mediator of its seizure protection
ruled_out: Disfavoured, not ruled out (DISFAVOURED_BY_SIGN_PRECEDENT): that inositol monophosphatase inhibition contributes to the protection lithium gives in the Wwox seizure assay, or that this enzyme is a lever for it.
reason: The documented consequence of inhibiting this enzyme in rodents is a pro-convulsant effect that inositol reverses, which predicts aggravation, not the protection seen; the protection also appears in wild-type littermates, so it is not specific to WWOX loss. The precedent is an analogy from another model (the drug together with low-dose pilocarpine), not a measurement in the Wwox assay, so it disfavours the route and does not close the assay question; the same mouse paper also ran a pilocarpine model in Wwox mice, so the objection that the provocations differ is testable in the same system.
detail_full: Curated mechanism rows in ChEMBL list inhibition of both IMPA1 and GSK3A/B for lithium; the sign argument rests on three abstract-level references. The null/wild-type panels (N 6 vs 7 and 12 vs 8) show a lithium effect of about the size of the difference between the lithium and ethosuximide null controls.
reopen: Inositol add-back reverses the lithium effect in the Wwox-null assay (then the GSK3 attribution falls and the enzyme becomes a lever with an unexplained sign).

subject_full: DNA-damage-response inhibitors (ATR, CHEK1, WEE1, PARP1, ATM)
subject_label: Inhibitors of the DNA-damage response as levers
ruled_out: That an inhibitor of the DNA-damage response is a lever for a WWOX-deficient developing brain.
reason: No scenario in the record makes over-activity of this response the harmful process; if the response is protective and already reduced, an inhibitor aggravates it. It is held as a harm flag, not a lever. Competence of the response in post-mitotic WWOX-deficient neurons is unmeasured.
detail_full: Path B reached these five genes through 80 signed inhibitor family-gene pairs, none named in a need; evidence for the competence deficit is non-neural (murine B cell and cell lines).
reopen: A WWOX-deficient neural measurement showing over-active checkpoint signalling that harms the cell.

subject_label: An inhibitor of class I histone deacetylases proposed to lower the glucose transporter SLC2A1 through HDAC5
ruled_out: The chain as written: that this inhibitor lowers SLC2A1 by acting on HDAC5 in a WWOX-deficient neural cell.
reason: Its strongest documented actions are on other deacetylases than the one the chain needs, the single reference for the edge is a knockdown in non-neural cells, so the attribution fails as written. (The two transcripts also move in opposite directions in the organoid, but that is a descriptive ratio that says nothing about enzyme activity and is not a reason.) This says nothing about whether the compound is inactive.
detail_full: HDAC1/2/3 about 3-7 nM against HDAC5 200 nM (a 67-fold difference) in ChEMBL activity rows; organoid HDAC5 0.81x with SLC2A1 2.67x.
reopen: HDAC5-specific lowering of SLC2A1 at concentrations that engage HDAC5, or class I inhibition changing SLC2A1 in either direction (then a different proposal).

subject_full: IOX1, KDM4C to HIF1A to HK2
subject_label: An inhibitor of iron-dependent demethylases and hydroxylases proposed to lower HIF activity through KDM4C
ruled_out: The chain as written: that this inhibitor lowers HIF activity without touching the HIF prolyl hydroxylases.
reason: In cells the compound stabilises HIF1alpha, the opposite of the intended effect, because concentrations that inhibit the intended demethylase overlap those that inhibit the prolyl hydroxylases; the intended target is also the least expressed family member in the WWOX-deficient organoid and absent in the human progenitor data. The route is the one that made another HIF-pathway agent a drop in IT9.
detail_full: Verbatim locator: the compound stabilised HIF1alpha at 0.2 mM relative to the control (Hopkinson 2013, partial full-text reading); ChEMBL PHD2 IC50 14.3-15 uM; KDM4C 11.7-17 cpm in the organoid.
reopen: A concentration window with H3K9me3 up, HIF1alpha unchanged and glycolytic genes down, reproduced by KDM4 knockdown (only if the role of HIF is first shown protective).

subject_full: CGI-1746, BTK to STAT3 to NPY
subject_label: An inhibitor of the kinase BTK proposed to restore NPY through STAT3
ruled_out: The chain as written: that BTK acts in the NPY-producing cell of the WWOX-deficient systems that carry the seed.
reason: BTK is barely detected in the WWOX-deficient organoid and is not in the human progenitor table (a table-membership fact, not a measured zero), NPY is near zero where it was measured, both edges come from other cell types, and the compound has documented actions on unrelated proteins. A proposal can be unreadable where it was generated.
detail_full: BTK 0.07-0.50 cpm in organoid libraries, not in the hNPC table; NPY 0.05-0.12 cpm in knockout against 3.2-7.7 in wild type; published off-targets of this exact compound include the sigma-1 receptor and the proteasome.
reopen: BTK detected in the NPY-producing cell class with NPY following BTK knockdown; BTK only in microglia moves the idea to another proposal.
